# HFrEF therapy

Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is defined by an ejection fraction of 40 percent or less.
Sacubitril-valsartan reduces cardiovascular death and heart failure admissions compared with enalapril.
SGLT2 inhibitors such as dapagliflozin lower heart failure hospitalisation regardless of diabetes status.
Evidence-based beta blockers are bisoprolol, carvedilol and sustained-release metoprolol succinate.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists need potassium and creatinine monitoring after starting.
Ivabradine is considered when sinus rhythm persists with a resting heart rate of 70 or more despite beta blockade.
An implantable defibrillator is advised for primary prevention when the ejection fraction stays at 35 percent or less.
Cardiac resynchronisation suits patients with left bundle branch block and a wide QRS complex.
